name: Mewing appliances

lead: Mewing appliances are palate-expanding or tongue-posture devices, including mouthpieces and plates, sold to supplement the practice of mewing, in which the tongue is held against the roof of the mouth in the hope of remodeling the jaw and midface. The practice comes from orthotropics, developed by John Mew.
It is a central idea in looksmaxxing forums, where users seek a more forward jaw, higher cheekbones and a sharper jawline.

paras: The theory is that sustained tongue pressure on the palate changes how facial bones grow. This is plausible in growing children with proper orthodontic appliances, but there is no controlled evidence of skeletal change in adults from tongue posture or over-the-counter appliances.

No randomized trials or controlled studies of mewing in adults were found; orthodontic bodies say there is no reliable evidence it reshapes the jaw. Forcing a tongue posture or wearing ill-fitting appliances can strain the jaw joint, shift teeth or cause discomfort. Myofunctional therapy supervised by a clinician has modest support for specific conditions such as sleep-disordered breathing, which is a different claim. The scholarly links below are the closest relevant research I could verify, not studies of mewing itself.
